answer_text:
Tessaway Freight has **65** carriers on file in the carrier master table (`tms_carr`), all of which are currently active (64 third-party carriers and 1 internal fleet).

ANSWER: 65

queries.sql: SELECT count(*) as total, countif(actv_flg) as active, count(distinct carr_id) as distinct_carr FROM tms_carr
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT carr_id) FROM tms_load_hdr WHERE carr_id NOT IN (SELECT carr_id FROM tms_carr)
SELECT carr_typ_cd, count(*) FROM tms_carr GROUP BY 1

matches.label: carrier
matches.definition: The carrier on a tender. A re-tendered load is delivered by the carrier on its final row.
rules: Loads hauled by Tessaway's own fleet are settled through the same tables and are treated the same way.

matches.label: margin
matches.definition: Margin is revenue less what was paid to carriers for the same loads.
rules: Carrier cost for an invoiced load is linehaul pay plus the carrier's fuel surcharge plus accessorials paid to the carrier. Cost follows the load into the period its invoice was cut.
Loads hauled by Tessaway's own fleet are settled through the same tables and are treated the same way.
Margin per load is margin for the period divided by the number of loads invoiced in the period.
Margin percentage is margin divided by revenue.
The carrier's share of a canceled-load fee is a cost in the period of the fee date.

matches.statement: A load is delivered when the carrier on its final row reports the final delivery: status DLVD. A canceled load does not count as delivered.

all_rules.statement: A customer is a parent account. It rolls up to nothing, and it is neither a shipping site nor a bill-to party.
A load is delivered when the carrier on its final row reports the final delivery: status DLVD. A canceled load does not count as delivered.
A load can be invoiced only when a signed proof of delivery is on file. An unsigned document does not count.
Revenue and loads belong to the parent of the site that shipped.
A load is booked on its first tender: the row that does not point to an earlier row. A re-tender is not a second load.
A load is one shipment, counted once: it has exactly one first tender.
A re-tender points to exactly one earlier tender. That first row keeps status RTND and is never deleted.
A shipping site rolls up to exactly one parent account, which is its customer.
The account on a load is a shipping site, and the account that pays is a bill-to party. Neither is the customer.
A test load or a voided load is not a load.

answer_text:
In September 2026, Tessaway Freight delivered 1,097 loads. Under the official customer contract on-time delivery definition:
- 38 late loads with shipper-caused delays were excluded from the measurement.
- There were 1,059 measured loads, of which 926 arrived on time at the final delivery stop.
- The official on-time delivery rate was 926 / 1,059 × 100 ≈ 87.4409820585458%.

ANSWER: 87.4409820585458

queries.sql:
WITH final_stops AS (
  SELECT
    load_id,
    stop_id,
    tz_nm,
    appt_end_lcl,
    arr_ts,
    DATETIME(arr_ts, tz_nm) AS arr_lcl,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER(PARTITION BY load_id ORDER BY stop_seq DESC) as rn
  FROM tms_stop
),
delivered_loads AS (
  SELECT
    h.load_id,
    fs.tz_nm,
    fs.appt_end_lcl,
    fs.arr_lcl,
    DATE(fs.arr_lcl) AS dlvr_dt,
    CASE WHEN fs.arr_lcl <= fs.appt_end_lcl THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS on_time,
    CASE WHEN EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM tms_stat_evt e 
      WHERE e.load_id = h.load_id 
        AND e.evt_cd = 'DLAY' 
        AND e.rsn_cd = 'SHPR'
    ) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS shpr_delay
  FROM tms_load_hdr h
  JOIN final_stops fs ON h.load_id = fs.load_id AND fs.rn = 1
  WHERE h.load_stat_cd = 'DLVD'
    AND h.test_flg = FALSE
    AND h.void_flg = FALSE
)
SELECT
  COUNT(*) as total_delivered,
  SUM(CASE WHEN shpr_delay = 0 OR on_time = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as measured_loads,
  SUM(on_time) as on_time_loads,
  SUM(on_time) * 100.0 / SUM(CASE WHEN shpr_delay = 0 OR on_time = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as on_time_rate
FROM delivered_loads
WHERE dlvr_dt BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30'

matches.label: on-time
matches.definition: Tessaway's official on-time delivery rate is the one its customer contracts define.
rules: A load is on time when the truck arrives at the final delivery stop at or before the end of the appointment window. Arriving early is on time.
A load that arrived late and has a delay the shipper caused (a DLAY status event with reason SHPR) is left out of the measure, top and bottom. It is neither on time nor late.
A load the shipper delayed that still arrived inside its window counts as on time.
Arrival and appointment are compared on the same clock: local time at the facility.
The rate is on-time loads divided by measured loads, over delivered loads.

Two other meanings are in use and are not the official rate: operations watches arrival inside the appointment window for every delivered load, shipper-caused or not; and the customer portal uses its own rule.
